model: BVPS compounding on adjusted (non-GAAP) ROE x exit P/B, cost-of-equity discounting (insurer/holdco route)

inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement (XBRL); not used in this valuation route
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (FY2025 10-K year-end; used as the compounding base instead of the noisier Q1/Q2-2026 quarter-end AOCI marks)
inputs.share_count_date: 2025-12-31 (FY2025 10-K diluted weighted-average; Q2-2026 actual is 610.2M, within normal buyback/vesting drift)
inputs.cost_of_equity_rationale: CAPM: risk-free ~4.2% (10yr UST, Sep-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta 1.5 (levered, cyclical alt-manager/insurer hybrid) = 11.5% base. Bull 10.5% (lower perceived risk if credit cycle stays benign), Bear 13.5% (compensates for the high-severity credit-cycle, spread-compression and retail-redemption risks the qualitative analysis flags). No WACC/net-debt subtraction -- Athene's insurance liabilities are operating funding, not net debt, and Apollo's own corporate debt is modest relative to the balance sheet; this is a pure cost-of-equity model per the insurer/holdco routing rule.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Apollo is a hybrid of (1) a fee-based alternative asset manager (Asset Management segment, ~30% of economics, FRE $2.5B FY2025 +23% YoY) and (2) a large spread-based retirement/annuity balance sheet (Retirement Services/Athene, ~60% of economics, SRE $3.4B FY2025 +9% YoY), plus (3) Principal Investing (~10%). Per dcf-methods/SKILL.md this is a two-row straddle (asset manager -> owner-FCF-style FRE multiple; insurer -> BVPS-compounding/residual-income). A true sum-of-parts was considered but rejected for THIS build: no segment-level FRE/SRE time series exists anywhere in this ticker's data (SEC XBRL does not tag the non-GAAP segment disclosures; no 10-K/earnings-supplement text was extracted for this ticker, only a single qualitative snapshot of FY2025 FRE/SRE dollar figures in APO_Analysis.json). Building separate FRE-multiple and SRE-book-value tracks off one data point per segment would be false precision dressed as sum-of-parts rigor. Instead this is a SINGLE CONSOLIDATED insurer/holdco-style BVPS-compounding x exit-P/B model (per SKILL.md row 'Insurer, holdco, compounder-of-book'), consistent with how FRFHF, IAG.AX and NAB.AX are treated in this folder. CRITICAL ADJUSTMENT: GAAP shareholders' equity and net income are dominated by AOCI mark-to-market noise on Athene's fixed-income portfolio (equity swung 10.2B FY21 -> 22.1B Q1'22 -> 14.4B FY22 trough on the 2022 rate shock -> 39.5B Q1'26 -> 21.0B Q2'26; GAAP BVPS CAGR FY21-FY25 is actually NEGATIVE at -2.3% despite the business growing by every operating measure) -- these marks reverse to par at maturity and are not economic losses. Per SKILL.md's explicit warning ('fair-value movements are not earnings'), the compounding rate is anchored on management's disclosed ADJUSTED (non-GAAP) earnings -- combined FRE+SRE, adjusted net income $5.2B / $8.38 EPS FY2025, +14% YoY -- translated into an implied adjusted ROE on FY2025 book (~21.3%) and faded to a mid-cycle terminal ROE (13% base, 16% bull, 10% bear) over 10 years, rather than compounding the noisy GAAP series directly. FY2025 year-end (10-K) book value used as the base, not the Q1/Q2-2026 quarter-ends, to avoid anchoring on a single AOCI-inflated or -deflated quarter. DATA LIMITATION: only a single-year (FY2025) adjusted-earnings disclosure was available (no historical adjusted EPS/ROE series was extracted), so the ROE fade path is a judgment calibrated to management's FY2026 guidance (FRE >20%, SRE ~10%, ~100bps/yr FRE margin expansion) and long-run mean reversion for insurance-linked alternative managers, not a fitted historical trend. Bear case carries the credit-cycle, Athene spread-compression, and retail-BDC redemption-gate risks flagged high-severity in APO_Analysis.json both through a lower ROE path and a higher discount rate and lower exit multiple -- risk priced once, not twice, in each channel deliberately (ROE fade = earnings-power risk, discount rate = required-return risk, exit multiple = market-sentiment/re-rating risk, which are three distinct risk channels for this business, not double-counting of one).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: adjusted_roe_terminal_fade (not a historical CAGR -- see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: GAAP BVPS CAGR FY2021-FY2025 is -2.27% (equity distorted by AOCI marks on Athene's bond portfolio, and share count nearly doubled at the Jan-2022 Athene merger), even as management-reported adjusted EPS grew +14% YoY in FY2025 alone and combined FRE+SRE grew to a record $5.9B. GAAP historical CAGRs are NOT used as DCF inputs in this build for exactly this reason -- see inputs.notes.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF/OCF series (from metrics_normalized) is not used either: OCF for a company with Athene's balance sheet reflects investment purchases/maturities and policyholder fund flows, not owner earnings, and is not a meaningful compounding base for an insurance-linked model (see dcf-methods/SKILL.md: 'deposits/policy liabilities are not net debt' and reported cash flow can be structurally noisy without signaling distress).

base.narrative: ROE fades from FY2025's adjusted ~21% toward a mid-cycle 13% as SRE growth (guided ~10%/yr) decelerates faster than FRE (guided >20%/yr off a smaller base) and spread compression at Athene continues at a manageable pace. Payout ratio rises from 24% to 38% as growth matures (consistent with management's stated ~10%/yr dividend-growth policy plus moderating buybacks). Exit P/B of 2.0x is below today's ~3.1x on FY2025 book -- moderate mean reversion as growth matures, while still reflecting the durable permanent-capital moat versus a plain-vanilla insurer (~1.0-1.3x) or plain-vanilla PE manager (no book-value multiple, FRE-multiple driven).

bull.narrative: Wealth channel, third-party insurance mandates and 401(k)/DC expansion scale faster than guided; credit cycle stays benign (2025's Tricolor/First Brands failures prove idiosyncratic, not systemic); ROE holds near 16% in the terminal years versus a 13% base. Exit P/B re-rates toward today's actual multiple (2.6x) as execution de-risks the growth story.

bear.narrative: Private-credit cycle turns: Athene net spread compression continues (funding costs +31% in Q4-2025 already flagged), realized losses emerge in asset-backed/direct-lending book, and the Apollo Debt Solutions BDC redemption gate (March 2026, ~11.2% of NAV requested vs ~5% honored) proves to be the leading edge of a broader retail-channel liquidity crisis that stalls the wealth-distribution growth strategy. ROE compresses to 8.5% at the trough before a slow recovery to 10%. Buybacks pause during the stress years. Exit P/B falls to 1.1x, a crisis-level multiple for an insurance-linked alternative manager.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance is achieved at a decelerating pace consistent with a maturing, still-attractive compounder: >20% FRE growth and ~10% SRE growth in FY2026 fade over a decade to a mid-teens combined growth rate as the AUM base scales and spread economics normalize. Adjusted ROE fades from ~21% to a mid-cycle 13%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Multi-market expansion (retail wealth, 401(k), third-party insurance mandates) delivers durable double-digit growth well past the FY2026 guidance window; credit losses stay contained to idiosyncratic names; Apollo's conservative underwriting stance ('principles not agent's mindset') lets it gain share from more aggressive competitors during any shakeout.
scenario_narratives.bear: The private-credit cycle turns broadly (not just Tricolor/First Brands), Athene's net spread keeps compressing, and the BDC redemption gate is the first sign of a structural liquidity mismatch across Apollo's whole semi-liquid retail platform, forcing a slowdown in the wealth-channel growth strategy that management has staked FY2026-2027 guidance on.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Not skewed further toward bear despite the high-severity risks (credit cycle, spread compression, redemption gates) because Apollo's own disclosed direct exposure to the riskiest pockets (software loans, subprime auto) is limited, and the permanent-capital structure of Athene is a genuine structural buffer versus a pure-play credit manager facing the same cycle.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Apollo is valued as an insurance-linked alternative-asset compounder, not a conventional owner-FCF business: Athene's permanent capital base and the fee-related-earnings engine are best captured by compounding book value at a management-disclosed ADJUSTED return on equity (stripping AOCI/fair-value noise that dominates GAAP net income and equity) and capitalizing the resulting book value at an exit price-to-book multiple, discounted at the cost of equity. This avoids two errors the routing rules exist to prevent: treating Athene's insurance liabilities as net debt, and treating AOCI mark-to-market swings as real earnings or capital destruction.
key_risks_to_valuation: No segment-level (FRE/SRE) historical time series was available in this ticker's extracted data -- the ROE fade path is calibrated to a single FY2025 disclosure point plus FY2026 guidance, not a fitted trend; a future rebuild with the earnings-supplement PDFs extracted could sharpen this materially
Private-credit cycle turn (Tricolor/First Brands-style failures broadening) would hit both FRE-driving origination volumes and Athene's asset book simultaneously
Athene net spread compression (funding costs +31% in Q4-2025) could persist longer or deeper than the base case assumes
The March-2026 Apollo Debt Solutions BDC redemption gate is a live signal of retail-channel liquidity mismatch that could stall the wealth-distribution growth thesis central to the bull case

Exit P/B is inherently a market-sentiment assumption; alternative-manager multiples have compressed sharply sector-wide in 2026 (Blue Owl -41% YTD) which argues the base-case 2.0x could still be too generous if sentiment stays impaired

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 99.56-153.29
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL via research/APO/Reports/APO_Metrics.csv and APO.duckdb core_metrics (no PDFs/Extracted text available for this ticker; FRE/SRE segment figures are non-GAAP and not XBRL-tagged)
data_sources.qualitative: research/APO/Reports/APO_Analysis.json (2026-09-25), citing FY2025 earnings release (Feb-2026) and Q3-2025 10-Q commentary

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
